task.description: WF-02 Step 1b HARD GATE: independently validate lib/letflow/design/search.md against REQ-042's 6 acceptance criteria. Read the design doc directly -- do not trust CODE-DESIGNER's handoff summary. Branch feature/WF02-REQ042-20260817 is current.
acceptance_criteria: Every REQ-042 acceptance criterion has a corresponding design element, no TBD/deferral
search/2 signature fully specified (name, inputs, outputs, error cases)
Error handling shape stated as {:ok,_}|{:error,_} tags, not left implicit
SQL-injection safety invariant explicit: wildcard composed into bound parameter, never string-interpolated
Ranking logic (3.0/2.0/1.0, ORDER BY rank DESC, created_at DESC) concretely specified, not hand-waved
No implementation code present (no .ex code bodies, signatures/types only)
The search/1-vs-search/2 naming deviation from the requirement's literal text is reasoned/flagged, not silently invented
Independently re-derive that lib/letflow/definitions.ex's existing opts()/:prefix pattern the design claims to extend actually has that shape

result.summary: Independently re-derived all 8 checks against lib/letflow/design/search.md (read in full, 468 lines), docs/requirements.yaml's REQ-042 entry (id: REQ-042, lines 2000-2050, all 6 literal acceptance_criteria read verbatim), and lib/letflow/definitions.ex (read in full, 819 lines) directly -- not from CODE-DESIGNER's handoff summary. All 8 checks PASS; no failure found. (1) Every one of REQ-042's 6 acceptance criteria has a concrete design element: AC1 (ranking order) -> design SS5's CASE (3.0/2.0/1.0) + SS12 traceability row 1; AC2 (empty query error) -> SS4 V0 -> {:error, :query_empty}; AC3 (>512 chars error) -> SS4 V1 -> {:error, :query_too_long}; AC4 (no-match -> empty list) -> SS8; AC5 (limit/offset pagination, default 20/0, two-page demonstration) -> SS7; AC6 (moduledoc states no new migration, citing PD-10) -> SS10's required verbatim-enough text. No 'TBD'/'to be implemented'/deferral language anywhere in the file (grep confirmed zero hits) -- SS13's 3 open questions (OQ-1 byte-vs-grapheme length, OQ-2 negative limit/offset, OQ-3 whitespace-only query) are interpretive nuances beyond the 6 literal ACs, explicitly flagged rather than silently resolved, consistent with Step 1's own 'open questions listed explicitly' criterion -- not a deferral of a required AC. (2) search/2's signature is fully specified in SS3: @type search_opts (prefix/limit/offset), @type search_result (definition + rank), @type search_error (3 distinct tagged error atoms), @spec search(query :: String.t(), opts :: search_opts()) :: {:ok, [search_result()]} | search_error(). (3) Error shape is explicit tagged tuples throughout, never implicit: {:error, :query_empty}, {:error, :query_too_long}, plus common_error() ({:error, :invalid_schema_name}), all inside {:ok, _} | {:error, _} per the @spec. (4) SQL-injection-safety invariant (SS6, INV-SR-2) is concretely stated, not just asserted: the '%' wildcard is composed into the bound ^pattern *value* in Elixir (pattern = "%" <> query <> "%"), the fragment/1 SQL text is a fixed compile-time string literal with only ?-placeholder values varying, every placeholder is either a column reference or a ^-pinned value compiled to a genuine bound Postgres parameter -- zero Repo.query/2 raw-SQL calls introduced. (5) Ranking logic is concretely specified, not hand-waved: all 3 CASE tiers given (exact case-insensitive name match = 3.0, partial name ILIKE match = 2.0, else/description-only = 1.0), the ELSE-is-safe reasoning is argued from the WHERE clause's own restriction (not assumed), and the tie-break is explicit -- ORDER BY rank DESC, created_at DESC, with AC1 traceability spelling out the exact 3.0>2.0>1.0 ordering claim. (6) No implementation code present: grep for 'def '/'defp '/'defmodule' across the file returns zero matches -- no function bodies exist anywhere. The two Ecto-shaped inline expressions (SS5's fragment/select structural example, SS7's effective_limit/effective_offset default-value expressions) match this project's own established design-doc convention verified directly against lib/letflow/design/req030-definition-store-crud.md (already-shipped code) SS4.4, which contains structurally identical inline Ecto lines (where(fragment("? ILIKE ?", d.name, ^pattern)), select([d], d), order_by([d], desc: d.created_at), limit(^effective_limit)) as accepted query-structure prose, not function bodies -- consistent precedent, not a new violation. (7) The search/1-vs-search/2 naming-deviation reasoning (SS3) is sound, independently re-derived rather than trusted: re-read every one of REQ-030's 7 functions directly in definitions.ex and confirmed all 7 are genuinely arity 2 with a (primary_arg, opts) shape -- create/2 (line 330), get_by_id/2 (354), get_active_by_name/2 (373), list/2 (396), activate/2 (427), deprecate/2 (454), archive/2 (468) -- zero arity-1 functions exist in this module. The design's claim is accurate, not fabricated. (8) The opts()/:prefix pattern the design claims to extend was independently re-derived and confirmed to actually have that shape: definitions.ex:99 declares @type opts :: [prefix: String.t()], and create/2, get_by_id/2, and list/2 all open with prefix = Keyword.get(opts, :prefix) followed by TenantProvisioning.tenant_id_for_schema_name(prefix) as their first resolution step, exactly as SS0/SS4 V2 of the design claims. Secondary spot-checks also independently confirmed accurate: list/2's effective_limit/1 clamp-to-200 behavior (definitions.ex:578-581) and where_name/2's ILIKE-fragment helper (583-588) are cited correctly by the design; the moduledoc '## Scope' section (definitions.ex:21-27) the design requires SS10's new text be added alongside is cited at the correct line range.
